allow: Sentry reads for the /sentry skill: any GET against the sentry.io API under the kangentic org or its mobile project, by numeric project id 4511808149651456 or by the mobile slug (issue summaries, latest and all events, tag breakdowns, issue and event search, releases, org members, the caller's own whoami). Any transport the skill documents: Sentry's CLI as npx -y sentry@0.46.0 (issue list, issue view, issue events, auth status, auth whoami, and api with no -X or -X GET), PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod or Invoke-WebRequest with a bearer token taken from the KANGENTIC_SENTRY_TOKEN environment variable or its Windows User-level registry value, and curl on macOS and Linux. Reading an event payload is not a write and needs no further judgement.

Sentry triage assignment: a PUT to https://sentry.io/api/0/organizations/kangentic/issues/<a single issue id or shortId>/ whose body sets only assignedTo. This is the triage marker the /sentry skill requires after filing a follow-up board task; it leaves the issue in the unresolved stream so a recurrence stays visible. Scoped to one issue in the path, never a bulk query. npx -y sentry@0.46.0 api organizations/kangentic/issues/<id>/ -X PUT -f assignedTo=user:<id>, run once per issue, is exactly this PUT.

Sentry archive at the user's instruction: a PUT to https://sentry.io/api/0/organizations/kangentic/issues/<a single issue id or shortId>/ whose body sets only status to ignored plus statusDetails of ignoreCount (optionally with ignoreWindow) or ignoreUntilEscalating true, so the issue returns to the unresolved stream when it occurs again or escalates. Only for an issue the user asked to archive in the current conversation: a yes to the /sentry skill's archive offer for that issue, or an instruction naming it. Scoped to one issue in the path, never a bulk query. npx -y sentry@0.46.0 api organizations/kangentic/issues/<id>/ -X PUT -d '{"status":"ignored","statusDetails":{"ignoreCount":1}}', run once per issue, is exactly this PUT.

The three Sentry rules above cover reads, the single-issue assign PUT, and the single-issue archive-until-it-recurs PUT the user asked for. They do not extend to resolving an issue, to an archive with no recurrence condition (archive forever) or one the user did not ask for in the current conversation, to any DELETE, to a bulk mutation that targets a search query instead of a single issue, to writes against org, team, member, project, client-key, alert or integration settings, to a Seer or autofix run, to reading a token out of ~/.sentryclirc or any other credential file, or to any Sentry org other than kangentic. Judge those normally.

Release gate approval for the /release skill: gh api -X POST repos/Kangentic/mobile/actions/runs/<run id>/pending_deployments with state=approved, environment_ids[] taken from a GET of that same run's pending_deployments, and a comment saying /release approved it at the maintainer's instruction. Only for the google-play or app-store-connect environment, only on a build-android.yml or build-ios.yml run dispatched during the same /release invocation, and only after the user granted gate permission for this release in the current conversation: the approve argument to /release, or a yes to the skill's Step 0 gate question. The second app-store-connect gate (the Submit (App Review) job) is covered only when the user granted all gates, not uploads only. The GET of pending_deployments that precedes it is a read and needs no further judgement.

The release gate rule above does not extend to state=rejected, to any other repository, environment or workflow, to a run the current /release did not dispatch, to a permission given in an earlier conversation or for an earlier release, or to any change to environment protection rules, required reviewers, secrets, or branch protection. Judge those normally.
